newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Prospects of a surplus in 1996/97 in combination with slack end user demand pushed world market prices for white sugar lower. The December contract in London finished $3.90 lower at $309.00 per tonne, while March closed at $306.00, down $3.10. A Reuters report confirmed that the EU may have difficulties getting rid of its export surplus in 1996/97. According to the report spot EU premiums have fallen recently to around $9 over the December contract after around $12 two weeks ago, with further forward delivery periods such as March quoted at around $5 when more C sugar should be on the market. The EU is expected to have more difficulties placing its exports in 1996/97 due to the gradual erosion of its Middle East market by the region's new refineries and the absence of large scale Turkish buying, which supported values last year. On the freight market the first Cuban order emerged. Although the order was not confirmed, market sources cited talk that Nissho Iwai was open for 24,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Japan for early January shipment dates. The overal fundamental outlook remains bleak with apart from technical reactions no improvement in sight.

ROMANIA - The total amount of sugar beet harvested by October 25 was 1.64 million tonnes of which 629,016 tonnes have been processed. The average extraction rate at the factory was 10.3 per cent resulting in a white sugar production of 64,956 tonnes. Molasses output up to October 25 was 22,816 tonnes. The total crop area in Romania in 1996 is 136,680 ha and average beet yield so far amounted to 19.2 tonnes per ha. The 22 Romanian sugar factories, which take part in the 1996 campaign have a total daily processing capacity of 56,000 tonnes of beet.

SPAIN - Sugar imports in July 1996, the first month of the 1996/97 campaign (July/June) amounted to 37,863 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 28,559 tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 353,193 tonnes against 257,273 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in July 1996 were France with 25,516 tonnes whites against 18,706 tonnes and Germany with 2,418 tonnes compared to 5,097. Sugar exports in July 1996 amounted to 10,793 tonnes, sharply up from last year's 41,655 tonnes. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 208,130 tonnes against 195,960 tonnes in 1994/95. The major country of destination in July 1996 was Tunisia with 9,150 whites against 11,642 tonnes in July 1995.

BRAZIL - The total amount of cane crushed in the period up to October 16 amounted to 191.35 million tonnes, up from last year's 81.56 million tonnes, a rise of 6.0 per cent, DataNet AgriCommodities reports. Total sugar production in the period under review amounted to 8.74 million tonnes, tel quel, against 8.24 million tonnes in the same period 1995/96, an increase of 6.1 per cent. At 10.06 billion litres, alcohol production is also higher, although the increase (4.4 per cent) is somewhat lower than the one recorded for sugar. According to the Association of Sugar and Alcohol Industries of Sao Paulo state (AIAA), the 1996/97 harvest in the Centre/South is complete by 87 per cent.
Tunesia bought 13,000 tonnes of white sugar for shipment in June 1997 at a price of $346.50 per tonne, c&f.
